Which tables belong to which year?

YearCore focus
Year 1Pictures, equal groups, sharing and counting patterns
Year 22, 5 and 10, including inverse division
Year 33, 4 and 8, retaining earlier facts
Year 4All facts through 12 × 12, including 11 and 12
Years 5–6Retained fluency used in written calculations, fractions, measures and ratio

How the table gym builds stronger recall

01

Find a starting point

A short warm-up samples the year’s skills. Earlier gaps can lead to supporting questions.

02

Train what matters

Practise a focus table, written methods, weaker skills and a wider curriculum mix.

03

Remember it later

Mistakes get a replay. Earlier facts return on later days, as recall evidence develops.

The same multiplication family connects both orientations, but division evidence is tracked for the relevant divisor. A correct multiplication answer does not automatically prove an inverse division fact. Coach introduces up to three new fact families in a short match, combines them with earlier facts, and returns mistakes after intervening questions.

Choose multiplication, inverse division, missing factors or a mixture. A 10-shot match is a useful stopping point; a 25-shot option offers a longer mixed round. These are the academy’s training formats, not the official multiplication tables check.
